title: VendPoint Start-Up Item Par Sizing Worksheet
content:
Worksheet for the par of the item most recently added to a machine of the VendPoint Industrial Vending Program, re-sized in Corbett's start-up par review.

**The item.** The item is the one whose add entry on the machine's selection history carries the highest planogram request reference (Corbett issues these references in sequence); its add date is the date of that add entry.

**Counting months.** Whole months between two dates are counted as the difference in calendar months, less one when the day of the month of the later date is before the day of the month of the earlier date; a record counts in a stated number of months ending today when fewer whole months than that number, counted this way, separate its date from today.

**Line 1 — The item's units.** The item's units are the units of that item vended from the machine in the three months ending today, less the units of that item returned to the machine or credited for a vend error in the same three months, each record counted by its date.

**Line 2 — Days in the machine.** The item's days in the machine are the calendar days from the date of its add entry to today, counted as one when the add entry is dated today.

**Line 3 — Average per restock interval.** The item's average per restock interval is its units divided by its days in the machine, multiplied by 7 (the days in a week), and divided by the model's scheduled restock visits per week.

**Line 4 — Standard par.** The standard par is the item's average per restock interval divided by the model's low-stock trigger percentage taken as a fraction of one hundred, rounded up to a whole unit.

**Line 5 — The par.** To size the par, each method that applies first replaces the quantity of the standard par it names; the allowances that apply are then added together and added to one, the standard par before its rounding is multiplied by that sum and then by each share and factor that applies, and the result is rounded up to a whole unit only at the end.

The scheduled restock visits per week and the low-stock trigger percentage are the figures of the machine's model.

### Hypothetical worked figure

Inputs chosen for illustration: 50 units in the three months, 30 days in the machine, a model with 2 scheduled restock visits a week and a 20% low-stock trigger.

1. Average per restock interval: 50 divided by 30 is 1.6667; multiplied by 7 is 11.6667; divided by 2 is 5.8333.
2. Divided by 0.20 (20 as a fraction of one hundred): 29.1667.
3. Rounded up to a whole unit, only at the end: 30 units.

### Window check (hypothetical dates, today 20 May)

| Record date | Whole months to today | In the three months ending today |
|---|---|---|
| 21 February | 2 (the 20th is before the 21st) | Yes |
| 20 February | 3 | No |
